body:
### Problem

## Summary

After a large bracketed paste — or any sufficiently large burst of input — Neovim
can permanently stop accepting keyboard input. The screen continues to **redraw**
and honour **window resize**, but no typed key has any effect and the session must
be killed. A paste that triggers it is applied only **partially**.

The root cause is in the input buffer in `src/nvim/os/input.c`, which is compacted
left rather than used as a ring. When the buffer drains after being filled to
within 19 bytes of the top, `input_read_pos` and `input_write_pos` are left pinned
near the top and the space check that would rewind them can never pass, so all
further input is dropped. See **Root cause** for detail.

## Affected versions

Reproduced on `master` (v0.13.0-dev) and v0.12.x. The relevant logic in
`src/nvim/os/input.c` (`input_enqueue`, `input_enqueue_raw`, `input_get`) is
unchanged across these.


### Steps to reproduce

The reproducer talks msgpack-RPC to `nvim --embed` and drives the input buffer
directly via `nvim_input`. It floods the input buffer, waits for the editor to
drain it, then checks whether a subsequent `:qa!` is still delivered. It uses
short fixed delays to sequence the UI attach, the flood, and the probe.

Save as `repro.py` and run `python3 repro.py --nvim /path/to/nvim`:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import argparse, subprocess, threading, time

def u(n):
    if n < 0x80: return bytes([n])
    if n < 0x100: return bytes([0xcc, n])
    if n < 0x10000: return bytes([0xcd, n >> 8 & 255, n & 255])
    return bytes([0xce, n >> 24 & 255, n >> 16 & 255, n >> 8 & 255, n & 255])

def s(b):
    if isinstance(b, str): b = b.encode()
    n = len(b)
    if n < 0x20: h = bytes([0xa0 | n])
    elif n < 0x100: h = bytes([0xd9, n])
    elif n < 0x10000: h = bytes([0xda, n >> 8 & 255, n & 255])
    else: h = bytes([0xdb, n >> 24 & 255, n >> 16 & 255, n >> 8 & 255, n & 255])
    return h + b

def a(items):
    n = len(items)
    h = bytes([0x90 | n]) if n < 16 else bytes([0xdc, n >> 8 & 255, n & 255])
    return h + b"".join(items)

notify  = lambda m, p: a([u(2), s(m), a(p)])
request = lambda i, m, p: a([u(0), u(i), s(m), a(p)])

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--nvim", default="nvim")
ap.add_argument("--fill", type=int, default=16368)   # >=16368 wedges affected builds
ap.add_argument("--timeout", type=float, default=5.0)
args = ap.parse_args()

p = subprocess.Popen([args.nvim, "--embed", "--clean", "-n", "-i", "NONE"],
                     stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                     stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
stop = threading.Event()
def drain():                     # keep the server's stdout pipe from blocking
    while not stop.is_set():
        if not p.stdout.read(65536):
            break
threading.Thread(target=drain, daemon=True).start()

# --embed ignores input until a UI attaches; options is an empty map (Dictionary)
p.stdin.write(request(1, "nvim_ui_attach", [u(80), u(24), bytes([0x80])])); p.stdin.flush()
time.sleep(0.3)
# flood the input buffer with ESC (a Normal-mode no-op), then let it drain
p.stdin.write(notify("nvim_input", [s(bytes([0x1b]) * args.fill)])); p.stdin.flush()
time.sleep(0.6)
# probe: delivered iff the input buffer is not wedged
p.stdin.write(notify("nvim_input", [s(":qa!\r")])); p.stdin.flush()
try:
    p.wait(timeout=args.timeout)
    print(f"fill={args.fill} RESULT=ok (quit)")
except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
    print(f"fill={args.fill} RESULT=FROZEN (input dropped)"); p.kill()
finally:
    stop.set()
```

**Expected:** `RESULT=ok` for every `--fill`.

**Actual (affected builds):** a sharp threshold at `INPUT_BUFFER_SIZE − 18`:

| `--fill` | free tail space after fill | result |
|---:|---:|---|
| 0 … 16367 | ≥ 19 | `ok` |
| **16368** … | **≤ 18** | **`FROZEN`** |

`INPUT_BUFFER_SIZE = (READ_BUFFER_SIZE * 4) + MAX_KEY_CODE_LEN = 0xfff*4 + 6 = 16386`
(`READ_BUFFER_SIZE = 0xfff = 4095`, `MAX_KEY_CODE_LEN = 6`), so `16368` is the first
fill that leaves `< 19` bytes of tail space. A single `nvim_input` call enqueues at
most `input_space()` bytes, so fills larger than `INPUT_BUFFER_SIZE` saturate at
this same boundary enqueue rather than writing proportionally more.

A paste of roughly 40 kB into Insert mode or a `:terminal` reproduces the same
freeze interactively, because the burst drives the input buffer to the top before
it drains.


### Expected behavior

**Expected:** `RESULT=ok` for every `--fill`.

## Root cause

`src/nvim/os/input.c` keeps a fixed buffer that is compacted left, not a ring:

```c
#define INPUT_BUFFER_SIZE ((READ_BUFFER_SIZE * 4) + MAX_KEY_CODE_LEN)  // 16386
static char input_buffer[INPUT_BUFFER_SIZE];
static char *input_read_pos  = input_buffer;
static char *input_write_pos = input_buffer;

size_t input_available(void) { return (size_t)(input_write_pos - input_read_pos); }
static size_t input_space(void) { return (size_t)(input_buffer + INPUT_BUFFER_SIZE - input_write_pos); }
```

Two facts combine into the wedge:

1. **The reader never rewinds.** `input_get()` consumes input by advancing
   `input_read_pos` and returning; it does not reset the read/write pointers to
   `input_buffer` when the buffer drains (`input_read_pos == input_write_pos`).

2. **The only rewind is gated behind the same check that fails.** The left
   compaction that rewinds the pointers lives in `input_enqueue_raw()`, but
   `input_enqueue()` only calls it from inside
   `while (input_space() >= 19 && ptr < end)` (19 is the maximum number of bytes
   one `<x>` key form can expand to).

So if input fills the buffer to within `< 19` bytes of the top and the editor
then drains it completely, the read/write pointers end up equal and pinned near
the top:

```
input_read_pos == input_write_pos,  input_available() == 0,  input_space() < 19
```

The `input_space() >= 19` guard can now never reopen, so `input_enqueue_raw()` is
never called, the pointers are never rewound, and every further keystroke is
dropped. `input_available()` stays `0`, so the editor blocks forever in
`state_enter()` → `input_get()` and never reaches `vgetc()`. Redraw and resize keep
working because they run on independent paths.

Code paths that call `input_enqueue_raw()` directly — stdin reads
(`input_read_cb`) and internal mouse events (`input_enqueue_mouse`) — would still
compact and rewind the buffer, but these are not on the RPC keyboard path, so
keyboard input stays wedged.

The state is directly observable in a debug build once frozen:

```
(gdb) p input_write_pos - input_buffer             # e.g. 16368  (pinned near the top)
(gdb) p input_read_pos  - input_buffer             # equal to write => buffer empty
(gdb) p (input_buffer + 16386) - input_write_pos   # < 19          => gate can't reopen
```

## Relationship to #10865 (not a duplicate)

#10865 ("dangling paste") is a different bug in a different layer. There, the TUI
is stuck *in paste mode* because the host terminal never sent the stop marker
`ESC[201~`; it lives in the bracketed-paste state machine and can occur at any
payload size. This issue is in the server-side input buffer and does not involve
bracketed paste at all — the reproducer above freezes with a plain `nvim_input`
burst and **no `ESC[200~`/`ESC[201~` markers**, so `input->paste` is never set.

| | #10865 (dangling paste) | This issue (input-buffer wedge) |
|---|---|---|
| Trigger | a lost `ESC[201~` stop marker | input volume filling the buffer to within <19 bytes of the top, then draining |
| Needs bracketed paste? | yes — the paste protocol | no — reproduces with a plain `nvim_input` burst |
| Depends on payload length? | no — any size, if the marker is lost | yes — purely about buffered length |
| Layer / files | TUI paste state: `tui/input.c`, `vim.paste()`, `nvim_paste()` | server input buffer: `os/input.c` (`input_enqueue`, `input_get`) |
| Symptom after freeze | stuck in paste mode; later keys inserted as pasted text | keys silently dropped; `input_available()` stuck at 0 |
| Fix | recover paste state (check `nvim_paste` result, Ctrl-C cancel) | rewind the drained input buffer (below) |

The two are independent: rewinding the input buffer does not help a lost
`ESC[201~`, and paste-state recovery does not reclaim the pinned buffer. A large
paste is simply one convenient way to generate the input burst that triggers this
issue.


## Suggested fix

Rewind the read/write pointers when the buffer is empty, at the start of
`input_enqueue()`:

```diff
 size_t input_enqueue(uint64_t chan_id, String keys)
 {
   current_ui = chan_id;

+  // If the buffer has been fully drained, rewind the read/write pointers to the
+  // start to reclaim tail space. input_get() advances input_read_pos on read but
+  // never rewinds it, so a drained buffer left within <19 bytes of the top would
+  // fail the `input_space() >= 19` gate below forever, silently dropping all
+  // further input and freezing the editor.
+  if (input_read_pos == input_write_pos) {
+    input_read_pos = input_write_pos = input_buffer;
+  }
+
   if (keys.size > 0) {
     set_vim_var_nr(VV_USERACTIVE, (varnumber_T)os_realtime());
   }
```

When the buffer is empty there is nothing to move, so the reset is a no-op and is
therefore safe, and it guarantees the space gate can always reopen. The non-empty
case needs no change: while `input_available() > 0` the editor keeps consuming
until the buffer drains, after which this reset applies.

With the patch, the reproducer above returns `RESULT=ok` for all `--fill` values
(verified up to 100000), and interactive large pastes no longer freeze the editor.

## Recovering a live frozen session (workaround)

The wedged buffer is empty, so resetting the two pointers is lossless. In a debug
build:

```
(gdb) set var input_read_pos = input_buffer
(gdb) set var input_write_pos = input_buffer
(gdb) continue
```

Then press any key; input resumes. (Keys typed while frozen were dropped and are
not recovered.) On my stripped build of 0.12.3 AppImage, this translates to:
```
(gdb)   set $base = (unsigned long)&got_int - 0x78dc1a
(gdb)   set $buf  = (char*)($base + 0x790900)
(gdb)   set *(char**)($base + 0x784fe0) = $buf
(gdb)   set *(char**)($base + 0x784fe8) = $buf
(gdb) c
```
which successfully rescues the session that was destroyed by a long interactive paste.

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

0.12.3, 0.13.0

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

N/A

### Operating system/version

debian 13, ubuntu 26.04

### Terminal name/version

N/A

### $TERM environment variable

N/A

### Installation

compiled from source & and appImage

Your patch looks small so we'd be happy to try it. Ideally with a test.

I didn't read the whole analysis but also keep in mind https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/10865

> Your patch looks small so we'd be happy to try it. Ideally with a test.
> 
> I didn't read the whole analysis but also keep in mind [#10865](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/10865)

Thanks — I don't think this is #10865. That one is a *dangling paste*: the TUI stuck in paste-mode because `ESC[201~` was lost, recovered via `nvim_paste([''],3)`, and it depends on the paste protocol/markers (can happen at any size).

This report is in a different layer and doesn't involve bracketed paste at all. The attached reproducer freezes by flooding `nvim_input` with plain ESC bytes — **no `ESC[200~/201~`, `input->paste` never set** — with a sharp boundary at `INPUT_BUFFER_SIZE − 18` (fill=16368). Root cause is in `os/input.c`: `input_get()` advances `input_read_pos` but never rewinds it, and the only rewind (in `input_enqueue_raw()`) is gated behind `input_enqueue()`'s `input_space() >= 19` check. Once the buffer drains while pinned within 19 bytes of the top, that gate can never reopen and all input is silently dropped (`input_available()` stuck at 0). A large paste is just one way to generate the burst. One-line fix + `--embed` reproducer above.

title: Editor permanently stops accepting input after a large paste / input burst
